playbooks.modelsUpdateHint: Compares the models your playbooks pick with what each CLI offers now. A swap keeps the same family (gpt-6-sol → gpt-6.1-sol, claude-sonnet-5 → claude-sonnet-5-5) and changes every place that picks the old one; the older model stays in the list.
playbooks.modelsUpdateChecking: Checking the models each provider offers…
playbooks.modelsUpdateUnsupported: This copy of the editor cannot read the model list; update Coding Opus or Coding Agent 2.
playbooks.modelsUpdateNone: Your playbooks already pick the newest model of each family.
playbooks.modelsUpdateCheckedAt: Checked at {time}: {count} models from the CLIs and the price table.
playbooks.modelsUpdateApplied: Applied. The playbooks save on their own; Undo reverts it.
playbooks.modelsUpdateAdditionsHint: Adding a model only lists it, so tiers and phases can pick it.
playbooks.modelsUpdatePriceOnly: {providers}: no model list from the CLI, so the skill's price table stands in.
playbooks.restoreFailed: Could not restore the previous version
prefs.routingPresetEconomyDesc: Cheapest roles first: a Haiku scout, a read-only Codex, and a Codex builder for the rest.
prefs.routingPresetBalancedDesc: Cheap roles for light work, Sonnet for the rest, Opus for deep tasks while its quota has room.
prefs.routingPresetPerformanceDesc: Sonnet by default and Opus for deep tasks; Codex backs up Claude.
playbooks.accountsHint: A worker starts on the first account with room below the stop line. When an account hits its usage limit, the runner retries the worker on the next one.
playbooks.accountsOnlyDefault: Only the CLI's own login so far. Add another account to give workers somewhere to go when it runs out.
playbooks.accountsManage: Add or remove accounts in Coding Agent 2 (Settings > AI Provider Accounts), or in a terminal with orchestrate.py account add. Both show up here and in the skill.
playbooks.accountsUnsupported: This copy of the editor cannot read accounts; update Coding Opus or Coding Agent 2.
playbooks.accountNotReady: Not ready: use this account once in Coding Agent 2 first.
playbooks.sourceCustom: The skill plans with your copy.
playbooks.sourceBundled: The skill plans with its bundled playbooks. Saving writes your own copy.
playbooks.drawerHint: The planner reads this before it plans or delegates.
playbooks.plannerHint: delegates one task at a time
playbooks.question: {text}?
playbooks.rulesHint: Checked top to bottom; the first match wins.
playbooks.rulesHintLow: If the provider it lands on is low on tokens, the role still moves to the next provider in the order on the same tier.
playbooks.leadHint: This phase runs in your own session; the tier says which model to start the lead on.
playbooks.implicitHint: The dashed “{condition}” box comes from the rule for every role; add a condition for it here to override it.
playbooks.gateHint: You check this yourself after the phase. On fail, the escalation below runs once per unit, then the check runs again.
playbooks.roleUnused: No rule routes here; it only serves as a fallback.
playbooks.fallbackHint: A read-only role can only fall back to a read-only role.
playbooks.whichRoleHint: Checked top to bottom; the first rule that matches picks the role. Empty kind and effort means any task.
playbooks.gateToggle: only while a quota window has room
playbooks.tiersHint: Providers in the order this profile tries them. Click one to change its models.
playbooks.globalHintBase: Apply to every role in every playbook unless a role has its own condition.
playbooks.globalHintProfile: Changes here apply to the {profile} profile only.
playbooks.planEndsHint: Quota is spare when a plan ends before its cycle resets, or the cycle resets soon with enough left. Leave a date empty when the plan renews.
playbooks.whenLow.switch: same tier on the next provider
playbooks.allLow.ask: run, and suggest waiting for a reset
playbooks.allLow.runCheapest: run on the cheapest tier, flagged
playbooks.whenSpare.spendStrong: spend it on the strong tier
playbooks.readOnlyNo: no: the runner cannot enforce read-only here, so scouts skip it
playbooks.usageNotRead: not read by Coding Agent yet; the planner asks you
playbooks.orderHint: Tried {position} of {total}. A role on auto takes the first provider that can run it; a low provider hands over to the next.
playbooks.routeGatewayHint: Coding Agent points this CLI at the local gateway; model names then go to whatever the gateway maps them to.
playbooks.modelsFound: Models the planner found for this CLI.
playbooks.modelsNone: No model list was recorded; the CLI picks its default unless you name one.
playbooks.routePanelHint: A local gateway on the model traffic path, not a worker. Coding Agent starts it and points a CLI at it; the planner never starts, installs or reconfigures it.
playbooks.routingSameAsPrefs: The same presets as Preferences → Orchestration.
playbooks.traceSpent: {provider} quota would be lost, spent on {tier}
playbooks.traceAllLow.ask: Every provider is low: work runs and the result suggests waiting for a reset.
playbooks.traceAllLow.runCheapest: Every provider is low: work runs on the cheapest tier, flagged.
playbooks.traceAllLow.block: Every provider is low: new work is refused.
playbooks.traceSpare: {provider}: {why}, so {percent}% of it would be lost.
playbooks.setupBundled: Bundled defaults. Ask the planner to set up orchestration: it checks which CLIs, models and routes you have, proposes base, savings and aggressive profiles, and saves them once you approve.
playbooks.setupDone: The planner found {providers} providers and built {profiles} profiles; you approved them on {date}.
playbooks.usageSimulatedTitle: {provider}: {detail}. Coding Agent does not read this yet; simulated
playbooks.unreadNote: Coding Agent does not read this usage yet; the values below are a simulation.
playbooks.spareWhy.plan: plan ends in {days}d, before its {cycle} resets
playbooks.spareWhy.planReset: plan ends in {days}d, before its {cycle} resets in {time}
playbooks.usageFoot: Low: a main window past {low}%. Stop: from {stop}% the runner refuses to start work there. Spare: {spare}% or more left on a weekly or monthly cycle that ends with the plan or resets within {hours}h.
playbooks.priceTitle: List price per 1M tokens: input / output
playbooks.port.no: When the condition does not hold
playbooks.tidyBlocked: Fix the problems first to tidy up
playbooks.blockHint: Drag onto the canvas, or onto a worker to add a model rule. Click to add it in the middle.
playbooks.problem.startUnconnected: Connect the start to the first step.
playbooks.problem.decisionNeedsYes: Connect the decision's “yes” to the step that runs when it holds.
playbooks.problem.decisionNeedsNo: Connect the decision's “no” to the next decision or step.
playbooks.problem.yesNeedsStep: “Yes” has to lead to a step.
playbooks.problem.noNeedsStep: “No” has to lead to another decision or a step.
playbooks.problem.stepNeedsNext: Connect this step to what comes next, or to the result.
playbooks.problem.stepsMustMeet: Steps of the same stage have to lead to the same place, or end at the result.
playbooks.problem.mixedStep: Only steps can run side by side; put a decision or check after a step.
playbooks.problem.gateNeedsPass: Connect “passes” to the next step or to the result.
playbooks.problem.failNeedsStep: “Fails” has to lead to an escalation step.
playbooks.problem.escalationOneNext: An escalation step leads to one place: another step, a check, the result, or back to its check.
playbooks.problem.escalationCheckEnds: A check inside an escalation ends at the result when it passes.
playbooks.problem.escalationReturn: An escalation can only go back to the check that started it.
playbooks.problem.loop: This connection makes a loop; only an escalation can go back, to its own check.
playbooks.problem.unreachable: Not connected to the flow, so it is left out.
playbooks.problem.duplicateId: Another step already uses this id.
playbooks.problem.skipMustMeet: “No” has to lead to the same place as this step, so the step is skipped when the condition fails.
playbooks.saveBlocked: Fix the problems in the playbooks before saving.
playbooks.decisionHint: When the condition holds the flow takes “yes” (right port); otherwise “no” (bottom port), toward the next decision or the last path.
playbooks.gatePortsHint: “Passes” (bottom) leads on; “fails” (right) starts the escalation, which ends at the result or returns to this check.
playbooks.startHint: Where every run begins. Drag from its port to the first step.
playbooks.endHint: Where the playbook ends. Connect the last steps here.
